title: Detect, Distill and Update: Learned DB Systems Facing Out of Distribution Data
note: Detect/distill/update pipeline for keeping learned DB components correct under distribution shift; single-node CPU or one GPU. Concern: no repo link found in the arXiv preprint (2210.05508) or via search

title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
note: Lookup-table mixed-precision GEMM for low-bit LLM inference entirely on the CPU - no GPU, no root, no kernel support needed, and 16 cores plus 125 GiB is a good target. Concern - the paper emphasizes ARM edge CPUs; the x86 AVX2 path is the weaker one, which is an opening for improvement rather than a blocker

title: Making Cache Monotonic and Consistent
note: Cache admission and eviction policy that keeps cached query results monotonic and consistent; trace-driven single-node evaluation

title: Demystifying and Improving Lazy Promotion in Cache Eviction
note: Trace-driven benchmark and improvement of five lazy-promotion cache eviction strategies plus two new algorithms; the archetypal cache-policy paper for this course and runs on libCacheSim traces

title: iRangeGraph: Improvising Range-dedicated Graphs for Range-filtering Nearest Neighbor Search
note: In-memory graph index for range-filtered ANN; single-machine C++

title: ST4ML: Machine Learning Oriented Spatio-Temporal Data Processing at Scale
note: Spatio-temporal feature extraction pipeline for ML - a data preprocessing/loading system. Concern: built on Spark; would need single-node local mode

title: GENTI: GPU-powered Walk-based Subgraph Extraction for Scalable Representation Learning on Dynamic Graphs
note: GPU subgraph-extraction pipeline for representation learning on dynamic graphs

title: Improving DBMS Scheduling Decisions with Accurate Performance Prediction on Concurrent Queries
note: Non-intrusive query scheduler driven by a learned concurrency-aware runtime predictor. Concern: the Redshift half of the evaluation cannot be reproduced, the Postgres half can

title: VectorVisor: A Binary Translation Scheme for Throughput-Oriented GPU Acceleration
note: A user-space WebAssembly-to-GPU binary translator/runtime (continuations for syscalls and recursion, register-file and bandwidth exploitation) running on a single commodity GPU. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: written in Rust (conda install needed) and evaluated on AWS GPU VMs for the throughput-per-dollar claim - on one A5000 only the raw throughput comparison is meaningful, not the cost metric.

title: GeDES: GPU-Driven Discrete Event Network Simulator
note: GPU-driven discrete event simulator - single GPU, user space, artifact available. Useful as a simulation substrate and its own optimization target

title: SNIP: An Adaptive Mixed Precision Framework for Subbyte Large Language Model Training
note: Adaptive mixed-precision LLM training policy; authors themselves evaluate with a pseudo-quantization proxy because they lack Blackwell, so it is GPU-portable. Concern: pretraining compute must be scaled to small models

title: JITServe: SLO-aware LLM Serving with Imprecise Request Information
note: SLO-aware LLM request scheduling under unknown response lengths and request dependencies - a scheduling-policy contribution that scales down to one GPU and a small model. Concern - compound-request workloads in the paper assume a larger serving cluster.

title: PCcheck: Persistent Concurrent Checkpointing for ML
note: Persistent concurrent checkpointing for ML training - user-space, works with one GPU and local NVMe

title: LITS: An Optimized Learned Index for Strings
note: learned index for variable-length string keys; user-space C++ benchmark against ART and HOT

title: Maya: Optimizing Deep Learning Training Workloads using GPU Runtime Emulation
note: Emulates the GPU runtime so unmodified training code can be profiled without real accelerators - this is precisely the kind of artifact that lets a one-GPU lab study large training configurations. No public repo found yet

title: A Comparison of End-to-End Decision Forest Inference Pipelines
note: Benchmark and optimization study of decision-forest inference across ONNX, TreeLite, HummingBird, lleaves, FIL, TFDF plus in-database UDF-centric vs relation-centric execution. All components install in user space via conda/pip plus a user-built PostgreSQL. Fits one CPU socket and one GPU. Concern: FIL/cuML path needs a CUDA build compatible with driver 535.

title: LakeHelm: Zero-Shot Lakehouse Advisor for Joint Engine-Format Selection and Configuration
note: Zero-shot mixture-of-experts advisor that jointly picks a lakehouse engine and table format plus its configuration. Concern: reproducing the training data needs Spark Trino and Presto installations

title: MetaStore: Analyzing Deep Learning Meta-Data at Scale
note: system for storing and analyzing deep-learning gradient metadata at scale; single machine with one GPU

title: Robust Query Driven Cardinality Estimation under Changing Workloads
note: Robust learned cardinality estimation evaluated on the CEB benchmark; PostgreSQL user-space build plus PyTorch on one GPU

title: PrefillOnly: An Inference Engine for Prefill-only Workloads in Large Language Model Applications
note: Storing only the last layer's KV cache drastically cuts GPU memory, which is precisely what makes long-input LLM work feasible on a 24 GB card; JCT-aware scheduling (shortest-prefill-first) is an obvious axis to improve. Concerns - the official artifact is a Zenodo zip of a vLLM fork (vllm_prefill-bowen-artifact-eval.zip) rather than a maintained Git repository, so it will not track upstream vLLM.

title: Learned Index: A Comprehensive Experimental Evaluation
note: Comprehensive experimental evaluation of learned indexes; CPU-only benchmark harness, a natural reproduction or extension target

title: Eva: Cost-Efficient Cloud-Based Cluster Scheduling
note: Cost-aware cloud cluster scheduler shipped with a large-scale trace-driven simulator alongside the AWS deployment; the simulator runs on a single machine. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - real-cloud validation is out of reach without an AWS budget, so any improvement has to be argued in simulation and with the paper's own cost model

title: Starburst: A Cost-aware Scheduler for Hybrid Cloud
note: Cluster/cloud-bursting scheduling policy driven by production traces with a released simulator; waiting-budget policy can be re-studied and improved by simulation on one machine. Concern: the paper also uses a 32-GPU private cluster and real cloud spend, so only the simulator half is reproducible here

title: GraphAr: An Efficient Storage Scheme for Graph Data in Data Lakes
note: Columnar storage scheme with custom encodings on top of Parquet; user-space C++ library on one machine

title: Resolving Packets from Counters: Multi-scale Network Traffic Super Resolution via Composable Large Traffic Model
note: Learned model (GPT-2-scale Granular Traffic Transformer tree) applied to a systems problem - synthesizing packet traces from counters; the repo has Train / Infer / data-processing directories and the models are small enough for 24 GB FP16. Concerns: training the full composable tree of GTT models may exceed a 10-week part-time budget on one GPU, so the project would likely target one or two granularity levels; training data must be regenerated from public pcaps.

title: JoinBoost: Grow Trees Over Normalized Data Using Only SQL
note: In-database gradient-boosted tree training expressed in SQL over normalized data; DuckDB-based, CPU-only single node

title: ADOC: Automatically Harmonizing Dataflow Between Components in Log-Structured Key-Value Stores for Improved Performance
note: Excellent fit. Pure user-space RocksDB auto-tuning framework that controls write stalls by adjusting thread count and batch size to limit data overflow. Evaluation is single-node RocksDB on NVMe SSDs - exactly the target machine. 16 cores and local NVMe are enough to reproduce the write-stall regimes. Concern: the paper sweeps several device classes (SATA SSD, NVMe SSD, Optane) and we only have NVMe, so device-sensitivity results would have to be narrowed or emulated with cgroup v2 I/O throttling.

title: BatchLLM: Optimizing Large Batched LLM Inference with Global Prefix Sharing and Throughput-oriented Token Batching
note: Offline large-batch inference with global prefix identification and throughput-oriented token batching, released as a vLLM 0.6.4 fork. Throughput-oriented offline batching is one of the few serving regimes that a single 24 GB GPU can study honestly. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/microsoft/MixLLM/tree/batchllm_vllm_064 .

title: I/O Optimizations in Graph-Based Disk-Resident Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search: A Design Space Exploration
note: I O-first design space exploration for SSD-resident graph ANN indexes with a page-level cost model and the OctopusANN composition; an experiment-analysis paper whose whole point is storage I O behaviour

title: Unison: A Parallel-Efficient and User-Transparent Network Simulation Kernel
note: Parallel discrete-event simulation kernel for ns-3 - entirely user-space CPU work, headline result is a 40x speedup on 24 cores, which maps well onto 16 cores / 32 threads. No root, no network hardware, distributed behaviour is simulated by construction

title: The Case for Learned In-Memory Joins
note: Learned in-memory sort/hash joins; CPU-only C++ with SOSD-style datasets. Concern: paper uses AVX-512 in places, our Zen3 has only AVX2

title: Cuttlefish: Low-Rank Model Training without All the Tuning
note: Automated low-rank training that picks per-layer ranks from observed stable rank - end-to-end training runs on one GPU on CIFAR or ImageNet-scale vision and small transformer models - concern - the contribution is closer to a training method than a systems artifact and full ImageNet training may exceed the time budget

title: QuickDrop: Efficient Federated Unlearning via Synthetic Data Generation
note: Headline metric is unlearning wall-clock time (463x vs retraining), i.e. a systems-efficiency claim, and FL clients are simulated as processes on one machine over CIFAR-scale datasets. Repo description names this Middleware'24 paper. Concern: the arXiv preprint appears under the earlier title "Efficient Federated Unlearning by Integrated Dataset Distillation".

title: Detecting Logic Bugs in Database Engines via Equivalent Expression Transformation
note: Equivalent expression transformation for finding logic bugs in DBMS engines - user-space testing tool driving SQLite MySQL PostgreSQL which can all be built or installed in a user prefix

title: Massively Parallel Multi-Versioned Transaction Processing
note: GPU-accelerated deterministic multi-versioned OLTP engine - a single-GPU user-space CUDA program with YCSB/TPC-C workloads. Concern - CUDA version of the artifact may need a conda-installed newer toolkit on driver 535

title: CertainSync: Rateless Set Reconciliation with Certainty
note: Rateless IBLT-based set reconciliation library with guaranteed (not probabilistic) success; evaluation is a single-machine simulation of communication overhead, no network or root required. Repo title matches the paper exactly. Concerns: contribution is closer to coding theory / distributed protocols than to the topic table's systems categories, and the motivating deployment is blockchain mempool sync - an audit may judge it out of topic.

title: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
note: RLHF dataflow framework combining single-controller and multi-controller execution; verl runs end to end on one GPU with 0.5B to 1.5B models using FSDP plus vLLM, so the API and scheduling layer can be studied at reduced scale. Concern - published results use 16 to 128 GPUs, so the 3D-HybridEngine resharding and placement search cannot be evaluated at paper scale on one A5000

title: SmoothE: Differentiable E-Graph Extraction
note: Differentiable (relaxation-based) e-graph extraction running on one GPU - a learned/continuous optimizer inside a compiler pass

title: FailLite: Failure-Resilient Model Serving for Resource-Constrained Edge Environments
note: Heterogeneous replication with smaller failover model variants, warm/cold replica placement and progressive failover across 27 small vision models - all fit comfortably in 24 GB. Concern - originally evaluated on a multi-device edge testbed; here it must be emulated with cgroup-v2-limited processes on one host (cgroup cpu/memory controllers are delegated, so this is possible).

title: SAS: Sparse Attention Synthesizer for Efficient Language Model Inference
note: Synthesizer that generates sparse attention kernels for LLM inference - a single-GPU kernel-generation contribution and a very natural improvement target. FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere. No code found yet

title: Laser: Buffer-Aware Learned Query Scheduling in Master-Standby Databases
note: Learned buffer-aware query scheduler; master and standby can be two DBMS processes on the same host. Concern: needs a full DBMS deployment and workload traces

title: BtrBlocks: Efficient Columnar Compression for Data Lakes
note: Columnar compression scheme for data-lake formats with a well-maintained C++ artifact; pure CPU, easy to benchmark and improve on this machine

title: EncoderForge: Generating Efficient SQL for Encoders in Machine Learning Inference Pipelines
note: compiles ML pipeline encoders into efficient SQL with a plan selector - an ML-to-SQL compiler artifact - concern: no repo located

title: IRHash: Efficient Multi-Language Compiler Caching by IR-Level Hashing
note: Multi-language compilation cache keyed on LLVM IR hashes; CPU-only build-system experiments, and clang/LLVM is installable per-user through conda. Concern: needs a sizeable disk budget for build corpora on the ~257 GB free volume

title: Insum: Sparse GPU Kernels Simplified and Optimized with Indirect Einsums
note: Sparse GPU kernel compiler lowering indirect Einsums through the PyTorch compiler; single-GPU, user-space

title: Revealing Floating-Point Accumulation Orders in Software/Hardware Implementations
note: User-space testing tool that reveals floating-point accumulation orders in BLAS/GPU implementations; runs entirely in user space on CPU and one GPU. Concern: it is a diagnostic tool rather than a resource-management system, so an improvement hypothesis would be about coverage or test cost

title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
note: Tree-based speculative decoding and parallel verification for LLM serving; the offloading configuration is explicitly single-GPU, so 7B-class models fit in 24 GB. AE repo is goliaro/specinfer-ae.

title: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
note: Cache eviction algorithm evaluated on 1559 open traces with a CPU-only user-space simulator (libCacheSim) plus patches to five production cache libraries; no root, no GPU, no network. Strongest fit of this venue-year. Concerns: the full trace corpus is large relative to 257 GB free disk so a subset is needed; throughput/scalability claims were made with 16 threads which matches this machine.

title: CSSTs: A Dynamic Data Structure for Partial Orders in Concurrent Execution Analysis
note: Collective Sparse Segment Trees, a drop-in replacement for vector clocks in dynamic concurrency analyses; user-space CPU-only library with a Zenodo artifact (10.5281/zenodo.10798906).

title: Unified Convolution Framework: A compiler-based approach to support sparse convolutions
note: TACO-based compiler that expresses many sparse convolution variants through affine index expressions - CPU and single-GPU code generation with a Zenodo and GitHub artifact - concern - builds a TACO fork with cmake and LLVM which is a user-space build but not a trivial one

title: IronSpec: Increasing the Reliability of Formal Specifications
note: Automated testing of formal specifications - Dafny and Z3 on CPU only fully user-space and CPU-parallel which suits 32 threads. Concern - proof/specification tooling rather than a performance system

title: Physical vs. Logical Indexing with IDEA: Inverted Deduplication-Aware Index
note: Deduplication-aware inverted term index built on Lucene and the Destor deduplication prototype. Single server, user-space Java/C++, HDD or SSD backing store - their own setup was one 128 GB Xeon box, comfortably below this machine. Concern: the artifact targets Ubuntu 16.04 (old Destor dependencies), so building on Debian 12 may need a conda/source toolchain; no system packages are strictly required.

title: Tamias: Feedback-Guided Systematic Concurrency Exploration for Transparent Distributed System Fuzzing
note: Feedback-guided systematic concurrency exploration for transparent distributed-system fuzzing (Purdue - Fonseca and Yongle Zhang, groups that normally release artifacts). Distributed fuzzing of this kind is usually driven from one host with several processes. Concern: no abstract or artifact public yet.

title: Million-Scale Text-to-Video Retrieval with Hyperdimensional Computing
note: Binary hyperdimensional video representation with a GPU Hamming-search inverted index - single GPU search system. Concerns: million-scale corpora may strain the 257 GB of free disk, and no code was found

title: zkStream: a Framework for Trustworthy Stream Processing
note: Official artifact repo from the authors' lab, described as "the artifact accompanying our paper". Rust, CPU-only proving and verification, benchmarked with NEXMark-style streaming workloads on one host. Concern: Rust is not installed and must come from rustup in $HOME; the repo ships a Dockerfile but cargo builds work without Docker; ZKP proving is memory-hungry, though 125 GiB RAM is ample.

title: CAFE: Towards Compact, Adaptive, and Fast Embedding for Large-scale Recommendation Models
note: Embedding-table compression for DLRM training/inference; single-GPU DLRM runs fit in 24 GB

title: Simple Is Better: Multiplication May Be All You Need for LLM Request Scheduling
note: A request-router scoring policy (KV-hit indicator x load indicator) - cheap to re-implement and to evaluate against the released Alibaba/Qwen usage traces. Concern: the real setting is several serving instances, so on one GPU it needs small models plus multiple processes, or trace-driven replay of the router only

title: Glider: Serverless Ephemeral Stateful Near-Data Computation
note: Ephemeral storage for serverless analytics that adds "storage actions" - stateful near-data operators plus an I/O streaming interface - so intermediate data is not shuffled through object storage. Core artifact is a user-space Java storage service (an Apache Crail fork) plus example applications in a second repo (https://github.com/CLOUDLAB-URV/glider-examples); shuffle/aggregation offload placement is a natural improvement target. Concerns - Crail is built for RDMA/NVMf hardware and Glider is normally driven by FaaS functions on a cloud platform; the project would have to stand on Crail's TCP tier and drive it with Lithops' localhost backend or plain processes, which is untested here

title: Segue and ColorGuard: Optimizing SFI Performance and Scalability on Modern Architectures
note: Segue uses x86-64 segment bases and ColorGuard uses MPK - both are unprivileged user-space features available on this CPU; Wasm toolchains build from source; concern: the linked repo is the benchmark harness and the compiler changes live in forks of wasm2c/WAMR/Wasmtime

title: Rethinking State Management in Actor Systems for Cloud-Native Applications (SmSa / SnapperX)
note: A user-space data-management layer over Orleans with new logging and concurrency-control algorithms for cross-actor dependencies - a runtime/concurrency artifact, no kernel or hardware dependency. Concerns - artifact README asks for Docker Desktop and AWS multi-region credentials; a single-host Orleans silo cluster is possible but needs porting, and .NET 8 SDK has to be installed into $HOME (no apt).

title: The Koala Benchmarks for the Shell: Characterization and Implications
note: Shell benchmark suite plus automation and characterization infrastructure; pure user-space CPU workloads, no root needed. Concern: it is a benchmark artifact, so an improvement project would target shell runtimes measured with it

title: GTX: A Write-Optimized Latch-free Graph Data System with Transactional Support
note: Main-memory latch-free graph store with transactions and concurrency control; multicore user space

title: SplitDF: Splitting Dataframes for Memory-Efficient Data Analysis
note: memory-footprint reduction for dataframes on DuckDB/Ibis; user-space Python

title: LLMFolder: Revisiting Constant Folding in Large Language Models
note: Constant-folding style parameter reduction for LLMs by linearizing activations - pure user-space model or runtime transformation, 7-8B models fit in 24 GB. No code found yet

title: ElasticFlow: An Elastic Serverless Training Platform for Distributed Deep Learning
note: DL-training job scheduler with an open trace-driven simulator - simulator runs on CPU; concern the physical testbed uses a multi-GPU cluster

title: Polaris: Enabling Transaction Priority in Optimistic Concurrency Control
note: Transaction prioritization inside optimistic concurrency control on one multicore machine - a scheduling policy with a released artifact

title: DROPS: Managing Serverless Resource Pools in Microsoft Azure Functions
note: Pre-warmed container pool sizing policies for Azure Functions driven by production allocation traces - trace-driven policy work explicitly in scope. Concern: check whether the artifact is a simulator or needs the real platform

title: Extract-Transform-Load for Video Streams
note: ETL pipeline for video streams that schedules model inference under resource limits; single GPU sufficient for a scaled-down stream count

title: BFTBrain: Adaptive BFT Consensus with Reinforcement Learning
note: Learned (RL) policy that selects among BFT protocols at runtime - a learned component inside a system, with an official, well-organized artifact. Replicas are user-space Java processes, so a 4-16 replica deployment fits in 32 threads with emulated latency. Concerns: the underlying subject is distributed consensus, which sits at the edge of the topic table; co-locating replicas on one host distorts the network/CPU contention that the RL features are built on, so results must be framed as single-host emulation.

title: AlpaServe: Statistical Multiplexing with Model Parallelism for Deep Learning Serving
note: Model-serving system: placement and parallelisation of many DL models under bursty request arrivals. The artifact ships a discrete-event simulator alongside the real serving path, so the placement-policy contribution can be studied without a GPU cluster. Concern: the real system needs multiple GPUs for inter-op model parallelism, so end-to-end reproduction on one 24 GB A5000 is limited to small models plus simulation.

title: WASIT: Deep and Continuous Differential Testing of WebAssembly System Interface Implementations
note: Entirely user-space: the tool and all six Wasm runtimes under test install without root and run on one machine. Concerns - it is a testing framework, so an "improvement" hypothesis would be about bug-finding throughput, coverage or oracle precision rather than system performance; the repo is small and lightly documented (2 stars).

title: Tribase: A Vector Data Query Engine for Reliable and Lossless Pruning Compression using Triangle Inequalities
note: Cluster-based vector query engine with pruning; CPU, single machine

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
note: Contiguous virtual KV cache using CUDA virtual-memory APIs - single-GPU; concern: the finest-granularity variant ships a patched nvidia-uvm kernel module that we cannot load, but the 2 MB-granularity path uses only user-space CUDA APIs

title: Bayesian Code Diffusion for Efficient Automatic Deep Learning Program Optimization
note: Auto-tuning search strategy implemented inside TVM/Ansor; runs entirely in user space on one CPU + one GPU, which is the paper's own evaluation setting. Strong fit: hypothesis-friendly (search-efficiency vs. achieved latency). Concern: full auto-tuning sweeps are long-running, so the 10-week budget must fix a small model set.

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
note: KV-cache fusion with selective recompute for RAG prefill; vLLM-based prototype runs on one GPU and a 7B FP16 model fits in 24 GB. Concern - some paper configurations use larger models and multiple GPUs, so the study must be scaled down to 7B class models

title: SplinterDB and Maplets: Improving the Tradeoffs in Key-Value Store Compaction Policy
note: LSM compaction policy plus maplets (mergeable resizable lossy maps) in a real embedded key-value store - a prime storage improvement target on NVMe. Concern: verify that the maplet variant is in the public SplinterDB tree and not only an internal branch

title: Strata: Hierarchical Context Caching for Long Context Language Model Serving
note: GPU-HBM / host-DRAM / SSD KV-cache tiering plus a cache-aware scheduler - exactly the 1-GPU + 125 GiB RAM + NVMe shape of this machine. Concern: no dedicated artifact repo found; the paper says Strata "has been integrated into SGLang", so the code is upstream (HiCache path) rather than a standalone release - verify before committing. arXiv preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18572

title: Dynamic Partial Deadlock Detection and Recovery via Garbage Collection
note: GOLF detects partial deadlocks by reusing the Go GC mark phase - a user-space runtime/GC change, buildable from Go source in $HOME; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (deployed internally at Uber)

title: Beyond Utilization: Energy-Conscious GPU Sharing for Inference Serving
note: Energy and carbon-conscious spatial GPU sharing for inference serving. Single-GPU colocation is the exact setting. NVML power readings and MPS both work without root on this machine so the measurement methodology is reproducible. Concern: no preprint or artifact link found yet.

title: High Performance or Low Memory? An Updatable Learned Index Framework for Time-Space Tradeoff
note: updatable learned index framework optimizing the time-space tradeoff - learned component inside a system - concern: no repo located
